koreterm 1.3.144

- Remote Desktop groups: right-click a Remote Desktop tab, Add to Group,
  New Group (or a group already open). The group's tab shows its sessions
  together in a square grid that fills it: 2 x 2 to start, 3 x 3 when a
  fifth joins, 4 x 4 at the tenth; free cells say so. Each session is
  under a strip with its name, Interact and Ungroup. The sessions are
  watch only until Interact (Ctrl+Alt+Home or Watch only gives them back);
  Ungroup puts a session back in a tab of its own, still connected, with
  its connection's own settings. Closing the group's tab puts every session
  back in its own tab: none is closed.
- A group is light: no sound, the fastest visual quality, compression on,
  and each remote desktop the size of its cell. Its tab's menu chooses the
  colors (256, 65 thousand or 16 million). koreterm measures its own CPU
  use every few seconds and, with more sessions or more load, shrinks the
  remote desktops and lowers the colors on its own; the header of the grid
  says what it chose.
- Save Group (the group tab's menu) keeps the group; the new-tab menu's
  Remote Desktop opens it again with all its sessions.
- Detach to New Window (a Remote Desktop tab's menu): the session moves,
  still connected, into a koreterm window of its own, with its tab strip,
  to put on another monitor. Its tab's menu then has Dock to Main Window,
  which moves it back, also without reconnecting.
- Hovering over a Remote Desktop tab shows its server and port and the
  user it signs in as; over a group's tab, how many sessions it watches.
- The tab in front has an accent bar along its top.

koreterm 1.3.143

- Remote Desktop tabs: right-click the tab, "Run Command on Remote
  Desktop...". Type a command (or pick Explorer, Processes, Services,
  Events or Restart) and send it to the remote computer's Run box, to a
  PowerShell window on its screen, or to PowerShell on the server through
  WinRM, which shows whether it ran and its output. "Open Task Manager"
  works even when the remote Explorer is gone. A restart or shutdown is
  asked about first.
- An applied update.zip is deleted, also when it was still in use while
  the update ran.
- Favorites: mark a profile with the star (Favorite) in its window, or
  with Favorite in the Profiles list's menu. Once any profile is a
  favorite, the new-tab menu (the arrow beside +) lists only the
  favorites; with none, it lists every profile as before. Run as
  administrator and Remote Desktop still list them all, and a favorite
  connection is listed at the top too.
- Notes for every kind of profile: Remote Desktop connections have Notes
  in their window, and the profiles koreterm finds (PowerShell, Command
  Prompt, WSL, SSH hosts) open a window with Favorite and Notes on Enter.
  A new profile based on one of them takes its notes along.
- Opening koreterm again (a shortcut, the Start menu, the exe) no longer
  opens another window: it brings the open one to the front. The jump
  list, +new-window and a launch that names a profile or folder still
  open a window.
- Remote Desktop tabs fit the window again after a move to a monitor with
  another scale, or a resize: the session takes the tab's new size instead
  of leaving bands of the terminal above and below it.

koreterm 1.3.142

- Settings > Profiles: "Sort A to Z" lists the profiles alphabetically;
  "Picker order" shows them again in the order of the profile menu (the
  arrow beside the tabs), the order Move up and Move down change.
- Settings > Profiles: "Hide built-in profiles" lists only the profiles you
  made; the ones koreterm finds (PowerShell, Command Prompt, WSL, SSH hosts)
  come back with "Show built-in profiles". Their rows now have a tinted
  background, so your own stand apart.
- Each profile has Notes: free text, any number of lines, in the profile
  window (Settings > Profiles > Edit). They are saved with the profile and
  never passed to the shell.

koreterm 1.3.141

- noctty is now koreterm, with a new icon: a core linked to its connections.
  The program is koreterm.exe; your config.ghostty and saved passwords stay
  where they are.
- Remote Desktop tabs no longer drop when left idle: the session now sends a
  keep-alive every minute. After a network drop the tab reconnects by itself
  at most twice, 15 seconds apart, and a login that fails is never retried,
  so a saved password that went stale cannot lock your account. When a
  session really ends, the tab says so.
- Remote Desktop no longer asks about a server whose certificate cannot be
  checked: connecting without asking is now the default. Settings > Shell has
  "Remote Desktop unverified server" to change it, and each RDP connection's
  editor can set its own.
- New in the window menu (the arrow beside the tabs): "Create Desktop and
  Start Menu Shortcuts" puts a koreterm shortcut on the Desktop and in the
  Start menu.
- A profile opened as administrator now starts in its own starting folder,
  not in the folder of the tab it was opened from.
- Tabs show their profile's icon: the program's own icon by default, or one
  you choose in the profile window (Settings > Profiles > Edit): a .ico,
  .exe or .dll file, an emoji, or none. The same window sets a tab color,
  drawn as a stripe along the top of the tab.
- A new tab, from the + button or a profile, now opens after the last tab
  (window-new-tab-position = current brings back the old place).
- A variable set with setx (or in System Properties) now reaches the next
  tab you open, as it does in a new window from the Start menu.
